name: Problem Elaboration Prompting (PEP)
executive_summary: Decompose and elaborate the problem's context before reasoning about it — accurate recognition of what's being asked, not just better reasoning steps, is the fundamental bottleneck for hard math problems.
description: Argues that prompt-engineering effort has mostly focused on improving the reasoning process (better prefixes, better exemplars) while neglecting a more basic failure mode: LLMs can mis-parse or mis-recognize an ill-formed or distraction-heavy problem statement before reasoning even begins, which misleads everything downstream regardless of reasoning quality. PEP inserts an explicit elaboration stage — decomposing and clarifying the problem context — before the reasoning stage, improving context modeling and parsing. Reports 9.93% and 8.80% gains on GSM8K with GPT-3.5 via greedy decoding and self-consistency respectively, with particular strength on problems containing distracting/irrelevant information, and composes cleanly with other prompting methods.
when_to_use: Mathematical or logical reasoning problems, especially ones with potential distractors or ambiguous phrasing, where mis-parsing the question is a plausible failure mode distinct from mis-reasoning about it.
when_not_to_use: Cleanly and unambiguously stated problems where context elaboration adds no new information.
known_pitfalls: The elaboration stage itself can introduce a subtly incorrect restatement, similar to the risk noted for Rephrase-and-Respond.

primary_source.title: Look Before You Leap: Problem Elaboration Prompting Improves Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models

variables.name: elaborated_context
variables.description: The decomposed, clarified restatement of the problem

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: A single LLM call (or a fixed sequence of them) with no external system dependency; running this template again at temperature 0 against the same model version should reproduce the same output.
